titleEn: Trampoline Fall - Spinal Cord Injury With Hypotension and Bradycardia

patient.name: Kyle Brandt
patient.affectEn: awake and anxious; lies completely still on his back on the wet grass, shivering a little; says he cannot feel his legs
patient.speechEn: full sentences, anxious but clear; cooperative; answers only what he is asked

scene.settingEn: Backyard of a house in Abbotsford, crew arrival about 1630. Cold, damp November afternoon, 6 degrees C. A round trampoline with a net enclosure stands on the lawn. The patient lies on his back on the wet grass beside it. A friend kneels behind his head holding it between his hands as the call-taker instructed, and a neighbour has laid a jacket over his chest. Nobody has moved him. The wet grass is slippery but there are no other hazards. One patient. If the candidate asks, dispatch will send First Responders.
hazardsEn: cold, damp weather - the patient is lying on cold wet ground and is shivering

bystanders.knowsEn: she called 911 and met you at the side gate; she leads you to the backyard and can open the gate for the stretcher if asked

has been holding his head still between his hands as the call-taker instructed; he saw him doing a front flip - he did not get all the way round and landed on the top of his head; nobody has moved him since; will keep holding until told to let go and will help with the roll if told exactly what to do
laid a jacket over his chest; nothing else; will help with the roll as an extra pair of hands if told exactly what to do

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: oxygen kit with non-rebreather mask and nasal cannula
hard cervical collars in several sizes
spinal immobilization device with foam blocks and straps
PCP: IV start kit and normal saline

dispatchEn: 1620 hrs. Code 3 to a house in Abbotsford. 19-year-old male fell from a backyard trampoline, landed on his head and cannot move his legs. The caller is his sister. Hospital is 20 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch update en route: the sister says a friend is holding his head as the call-taker instructed; he is awake, lying on the lawn and says he cannot feel his legs; there is no heavy bleeding. It is a cold, damp afternoon. Fire First Responders are not attending.
arrivalEn: His sister meets you at the side gate and leads you to the backyard. A round trampoline with a net enclosure stands on the lawn. The patient lies on his back on the wet grass beside it. A friend kneels behind his head, holding it between his hands as the call-taker instructed, and a neighbour has laid a jacket over his chest. Nobody has moved him. Bystanders say he was doing a front flip. It is a cold, damp November afternoon, 6 degrees C, and the wet grass is slippery but there are no other hazards. One patient.
firstLookEn: A young man lying still on his back on the wet grass beside the trampoline, shivering a little, awake and anxious. A friend kneels behind his head holding it between his hands, and there is a jacket over his chest.

primary.airwayEn: Clear. He speaks in full sentences.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 16, regular, adequate depth, chest rises symmetrically. SpO2 96% on room air if checked before oxygen goes on.
primary.rbsEn: Hands-on, without moving him: chest symmetrical, no bruising; abdomen soft and non-tender; pelvis stable; no external bleeding anywhere. Midline tenderness at the base of the neck and between the shoulder blades when palpated with his head held. If the groin is exposed, a persistent erection (priapism) is noted. Neuro (CSM): arms - moves both on command, strong equal grip, sensation intact; legs - no movement on command and no response to touch or pinch below the nipple line. Skin is given automatically during the RBS: warm, pink and dry below the nipple line; face and hands cool. Examiner notes - do not volunteer: report unprotected-search if the candidate rolls, sits up, lifts or strips him for the search without manual stabilization held.
primary.skinEn: warm, pink and dry below the nipple line; face and hands cool

history.ccEn: I can't feel or move my legs, and my neck and upper back hurt.

opqrst.oEn: I was doing a front flip on the trampoline, didn't get all the way round and landed on the top of my head and folded over. My legs went numb straight away.
opqrst.pEn: Any movement of my head makes it worse. Nothing makes it better.
opqrst.rEn: At the base of my neck and between my shoulder blades. It doesn't go anywhere else.
opqrst.sEn: About a five out of ten.
opqrst.tEn: At about 4:16, about fourteen minutes before you got here.

sample.sEn: I can't feel or move my legs, my neck and upper back hurt, and I feel lightheaded and cold. No chest pain, no belly pain, no trouble breathing, no headache.
sample.aEn: None that I know of. (If asked about ibuprofen specifically: "No, I've never had a reaction to it.")
sample.mEn: I don't take anything. (Only if asked about acetaminophen, Tylenol, ibuprofen or Advil today: "No, I haven't taken any." Only if asked about blood thinners: "No.")
sample.pEn: I'm healthy, nothing at all. (Asked about the pain pills - liver problems, stomach ulcers or bleeding: "No, none of that." If asked his weight: "Seventy-eight kilos.")
sample.lEn: Lunch around 12:30 and just water since.
sample.eEn: I was doing a front flip, didn't get all the way round, landed on the top of my head and folded over. I didn't black out, I haven't vomited, and I haven't had any alcohol or drugs today.

fe.generalEn: I felt fine until the fall. Now I'm lightheaded and cold.
fe.cnsEn: No headache, no confusion, I didn't black out. I'm numb and can't move anything below my nipples.
fe.cardiovascularEn: No chest pain, no palpitations. I'm lightheaded.
fe.giGuEn: No belly pain, no nausea. I can't tell whether I've passed urine.
fe.integumentaryEn: No wounds, no rash. I feel cold.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: My neck and upper back hurt. No other pain.
fe.eentEn: No problems with my vision or my hearing, no ear problems.

findings.headNeckEn: No wounds, no deformity. Midline tenderness at the base of the neck when palpated with his head held. If a collar has been applied it is in place.
findings.chestLungsEn: Symmetrical rise, equal air entry, no bruising. After the first 500 mL of fluid (PCP) the chest is still clear.
findings.abdomenEn: Soft, non-tender, not distended. Pelvis stable.
findings.backEn: Seen during the roll: midline tenderness between the shoulder blades, no step deformity, bruising or wounds.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: No deformity. No movement and no sensation below the nipple line (no response to touch or pinch). Pedal pulses present. Skin warm and dry.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: No injury. Full movement, strong equal grip, sensation intact. Radial pulses weak.

vitalsSets.skin: warm, pink, dry below the injury; face and hands cool

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: 6 min after set 1, packaged and warmed on the device, about 1642; neurological status unchanged
vitalsSets.skin: warm, pink, dry below the injury; face and hands warmer

vitalsSets.skin: warm, pink, dry below the injury; face and hands warmer

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan the collar, spinal immobilization device with blocks and straps, oxygen, blankets and extra hands, with early transport
triggers: bring the collar and the spinal device
plan extra hands for the roll
this will be an early transport

expected.actionEn: Recognize from dispatch that a head-first landing with loss of leg movement and feeling is a spinal cord injury: nobody moves him until you take over the head
triggers: head first landing with leg numbness
nobody moves him until I take the head
treat this as a spinal injury

expected.actionEn: Consider additional resources (First Responders) for the coordinated roll and lift
Anticipate a cold, wet backyard; PPE incl gloves
Verbalize hazards (slippery wet grass only), environment (cold, damp, outdoors), mechanism (head-first landing from a front flip on a trampoline) and number of patients (1)
triggers: mechanism is a front flip on a trampoline

expected.actionEn: Don gloves
First look: young man supine and still on cold wet grass, shivering, friend holding his head, awake and anxious
Approach calmly, tell him not to move, ask the friend to keep holding his head until you take over, and request First Responders
Assess LOC / AVPU: Alert
triggers: do you know where you are

expected.actionEn: Take over manual in-line stabilization of the head and neck from the friend BEFORE any movement or pain stimulus (head-first landing, midline tenderness and a neurological deficit = NEXUS positive) and keep it until he is secured to the device
triggers: manual stabilization of the head and neck

expected.actionEn: Assess airway while holding the head still - clear
triggers: he's talking so the airway is open

expected.actionEn: Assess breathing: rate, depth, chest rise and SpO2
Assess circulation: radial pulse is slow and weak - recognize it as abnormal, suspect hypotension and keep him flat

Rapid body survey hands-on WITHOUT moving or rolling him: search chest, abdomen, pelvis and limbs for hidden bleeding and other injury, and check movement and feeling in all four limbs; the search never costs him his spinal precautions
triggers: search the chest abdomen and pelvis
check movement and feeling in all four limbs

expected.actionEn: Note skin: warm, pink and dry below the injury, face and hands cool
triggers: skin above and below the injury

expected.actionEn: High-flow oxygen 15 L NRB (trauma with suspected shock), titrated to keep SpO2 at 94% or more
Position supine and flat, no sitting up, no recovery position; cover him with a blanket against the cold wet ground
Categorize as RTC (new-onset neurological deficit) and act with urgency
triggers: new neurological deficit makes him unstable

expected.actionEn: Packaged on the device, warmed and ready to be lifted onto the cot within 15 minutes
triggers: ready to lift onto the cot

expected.actionEn: Complete baseline vitals and the oral analgesia before the roll without losing the sense of urgency
triggers: vitals and analgesia before the roll
baseline vitals first then the roll
give the pain medication before we roll
the protocol is not a delay

expected.actionEn: Delegate effectively: partner fetches device and cot, friend and neighbour act as extra hands in the roll under your head control, sister opens the gate
triggers: partner, get the device and the cot
friend and neighbour, help with the roll
I'll lead the roll from the head
you two hold his shoulders and hips

expected.actionEn: Establish chief complaint: cannot feel or move his legs, with neck and upper-back pain
HxC/C: how he landed, time of injury, immediate onset of numbness, no LOC or vomiting, no alcohol or drugs, whether anyone moved him since
triggers: did your legs go numb right away

expected.actionEn: Pain score and character (neck and upper back)
PMHx
Medications incl acetaminophen or ibuprofen taken today and blood thinners
triggers: taken any Tylenol or ibuprofen today

expected.actionEn: Allergies incl any reaction to ibuprofen
LOI
Ask the questions that rule out each analgesic's contraindications (liver disease, ulcers or bleeding) and get his weight for the fluid dose
GCS with components (15: E4 V5 M6)
BP by auscultation - recognize a systolic pressure below 90 as hypotension and say what it triggers (keep flat, keep warm, oxygen, search for bleeding)
Pulse rate, strength and rhythm - recognize a slow pulse with low BP, not the fast pulse expected with blood loss
Respirations rate, depth and character
Skin hands-on: temperature, colour, condition above and below the injury
triggers: feel the skin above and below the injury

expected.actionEn: Pupils
SpO2 and confirm it matches the palpated pulse
Temperature - indicated after lying on cold wet ground
Verbalize that BGL is not indicated: alert, no diabetes, no altered LOC
FE - General health
FE - CNS (headache, confusion, level of numbness)
FE - Respiratory

Head/neck exam with the collar and manual stabilization maintained
Chest exam with auscultation, bilateral comparison
Abdomen exam for tenderness and distension (hidden bleeding)

triggers: check the back during the roll
run my hands down the back

expected.actionEn: Lower extremities: movement, sensation, pulses
triggers: movement and sensation in the legs

expected.actionEn: Upper extremities: movement, sensation, pulses
triggers: movement and sensation in the arms

expected.actionEn: Spinal management: sized hard collar applied without losing manual stabilization, foam blocks, body secured to the device and the head NOT taped (p.25)
triggers: secure the body then the head

expected.actionEn: Move him off the cold ground onto the device with manual stabilization held throughout the roll, neutral alignment, the back examined, and a blanket under and over him
triggers: examine the back during the roll

expected.actionEn: Initiate the Pain Management protocol only after baseline vitals, ruling out the contraindications of acetaminophen (hypersensitivity, liver disease, recent doses) and ibuprofen (NSAID hypersensitivity, GI bleeding or ulcers, anticoagulants, pregnancy) BEFORE the roll (p.58, p.68)
triggers: no liver disease and no ulcers

expected.actionEn: Administer acetaminophen 1000 mg PO and ibuprofen 400 mg PO with the 6 rights
triggers: right patient right drug right dose

expected.actionEn: Verbalize withholding Entonox: shock is a caution on p.65 and his BP is 78/44
triggers: no Entonox because of the hypotension

expected.actionEn: Verbalize the hypotension plan: SBP below 90 is treated (supine and flat, warm, oxygen to 94% or more) although the Hypovolemia indications are not all met - no blood loss seen, pulse 52, warm dry skin - and the search for hidden bleeding continues
triggers: hypovolemia indications are not all met

expected.actionEn: PCP: IV en route and a bolus of 20 mL/kg (78 kg = 1,560 mL, maximum 2 L) reassessed every 500 mL, target SBP 90
PCP: verbalize why TXA is not given - no physical findings suggestive of occult or ongoing bleeding, shock not shown to be from blood loss (p.78, p.54)
Reassess ABCs, CSM and all interventions after the roll and after each move
triggers: recheck the collar and the straps

expected.actionEn: Second full set of vitals within 5-6 minutes of the first and interpret the trend (BP still low, neurological level unchanged)
PCP: reassess BP and chest after each 500 mL, recognize the target SBP of 90 is reached and stop the bolus
triggers: systolic is above 90 so I'm stopping the fluid

expected.actionEn: Recheck movement and sensation after the move and tell the hospital at once if the level of numbness rises
triggers: tell the hospital if the numbness rises

expected.actionEn: En-route notification for a critical patient (spinal cord injury with hypotension)
Complete hand-off: mechanism, time of injury, neurological level and deficits, vitals trend and response to treatment
State the drug times and what was withheld (Entonox, TXA) with the reasons
triggers: Entonox was withheld for the hypotension
TXA not given because there was no sign of bleeding

expected.actionEn: Accurate PCR within 5 minutes with times, neurological findings and the reason Entonox was withheld

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate (or the partner on the candidate's instruction) takes over manual in-line stabilization of the head and neck from the friend, applies a hard collar, or starts spinal motion restriction (good act; also detected from the candidate's words)

candidate rolls, sits up, lifts or turns him, directs anyone to move him, or lets him lift or turn his head BEFORE the candidate or the partner has taken over manual stabilization of the head and neck; the friend's hold does not count as the candidate's control. Asking him to wiggle his fingers or toes or squeeze a hand, and light touch, are NOT this event

candidate applies a painful stimulus (a pinch or pinprick to test sensation, a sternal rub) BEFORE the candidate or the partner has taken over manual stabilization of the head and neck; the friend's hold does not count as the candidate's control

candidate (or the partner on the candidate's instruction) lets go of manual head and neck stabilization before the patient is secured on the spinal device with the collar on and the head blocks in place; applying the collar alone does not permit release

candidate searches for hidden bleeding after the low BP by rolling, sitting up, lifting or stripping him (for example rolling him to look at the back, or lifting the pelvis) without manual stabilization held and without a coordinated roll; a hands-on survey without moving him is correct and must NOT be recorded

candidate rolls or lifts him onto the device without a coordinated roll: the head is not controlled by one person who leads the roll, there is no call or count, or the body is not kept in neutral alignment (for example a casual drag or lift by the shoulders and legs)
candidate tapes the patient's head to the spinal device
candidate sits him up, props him up, turns him onto his side or into the recovery position, or tells him to sit up, at any time
candidate covers him or keeps him warm against the cold wet ground: a blanket, insulation, warming the unit (good act; also detected from the candidate's words)
candidate puts a blanket or insulation under him or on the device before he is lifted onto it - a blanket under and over him (good act; also detected from the candidate's words)
candidate gives or states an acetaminophen dose outside 500-1000 mg PO or an ibuprofen dose outside 300-400 mg PO (for example 2 g of acetaminophen or 800 mg of ibuprofen)

PCP orders a bolus volume that is not 20 mL/kg of 78 kg (about 1,560 mL, maximum 2 L) - for example a flat 1 L or 2 L wide open, a different per-kilo dose, or a volume computed from a weight other than 78 kg; saying 20 mL/kg with a maximum of 2 L and the weight is correct
PCP runs the saline bolus past 500 mL, or onto the next 500 mL, without reassessing the patient (BP / vitals / chest) in between

AFTER a systolic BP of 90 or higher (92/56) has been given, the PCP keeps the bolus running or orders more fluid (another 500 mL, the rest of the 1,560 mL, or wide open) instead of stopping at the target

drugs.doseEn: 1000 mg PO (guideline range 500 - 1000 mg PO; may repeat once after 4 hours - not within 4 hours of a prior dose; contraindicated in severe liver disease, hypersensitivity or suspected overdose). Given before the roll, after baseline vitals and the contraindication check; may be used together with ibuprofen.

400 mg PO (guideline range 300 - 400 mg PO; may repeat every 4-6 hours; contraindicated with NSAID hypersensitivity, active GI hemorrhage or ulcers, pregnancy or anticoagulants). Given before the roll, after baseline vitals and the contraindication check.
self-administered by inhalation - WITHHELD in this scenario: shock is a caution on p.65 and his BP is 78/44. A statement of withholding it is NOT drug:entonox.

vascular access en route, then a bolus of 20 mL/kg (78 kg = 1,560 mL, maximum 2 L), reassessing BP and chest after every 500 mL; target systolic BP 90 - the first 500 mL brings him to 92/56, so the bolus is stopped

2 g (2000 mg) IV push over 1 minute - NOT indicated: no physical findings suggestive of occult or ongoing bleeding and the low BP is not shown to be from blood loss. A statement that it is not indicated is NOT drug:txa.
drugs.indicationsEn: major trauma after initiation of the Hypovolemia protocol; signs of shock with a mechanism or findings suggestive of occult or ongoing bleeding - not met
drugs.contraindicationsEn: known hypersensitivity or allergy to TXA; more than 3 hours after injury; patient under 12 years; isolated TBI
drugs.cautionsEn: further hypotension if administered too quickly

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR: manual stabilization, hard collar, spinal device with blocks, blankets, high-flow oxygen and keeping him supine, flat and warm are all EMR skills, as are oral acetaminophen and ibuprofen for pain (only pyrexia dosing is PCP-only, p.58/68). Entonox is withheld (shock caution, p.65). No IV, no fluid bolus, no TXA, no Functional Enquiry - the hypotension is managed with positioning, warmth, oxygen and the 15-minute RTC clock. (Textbook label - not a BC rubric item: low BP with a slow pulse and warm dry skin below a spinal injury is usually called neurogenic shock; the BC guidelines do not use the term. Textbook caution - not a BC rubric item: some clinicians hold ibuprofen while occult bleeding is not excluded; neither monograph lists hypotension as a contraindication, so the rubric expectation is both oral agents.)
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds the 9-system Functional Enquiry en route, vascular access en route and a fluid bolus of 20 mL/kg (78 kg = 1,560 mL, maximum 2 L) reassessed every 500 mL and stopped when the target SBP of 90 is reached (p.54, p.48), because he is hypotensive and it is clinically indicated; the chest is rechecked at each step. TXA is not indicated without findings of occult or ongoing bleeding (p.78). (Textbook practice - not a BC rubric item: in this pattern of low BP with a slow pulse, more fluid does not fix the cause and risks overload, which is why the bolus is stopped as soon as the target is reached.)

sourcePages: Scenario tr-12 (data/practical/scenarios-2.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport, history, vitals sets 1-2 (set 3: PCP after the first 500 mL of the bolus), FE, exam, interventions, ongoing, handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 RTC criteria (new-onset neurological deficits; cool pale clammy skin secondary to suspected shock), p.9-10 Patient Assessment Model (spinal precautions before airway, survey interventions incl position and blanket, additional resources such as First Responders), p.11 Primary Survey Interventions (cervical spine stabilization with NEXUS or Canadian C-Spine indications; oxygen for trauma and evidence of shock), p.13 AVPU, p.25 Spinal Management (NEXUS / Canadian C-Spine; manually stabilize the head and neck, hard collar, spinal immobilization device, foam blocks, do not tape the head), p.29 (remove wet clothing and cover with blankets, take temperature if appropriate), p.48 (fluid bolus 20 mL/kg to a maximum of 2 L reassessing every 500 mL, target systolic 90), p.50 Oxygen Administration, p.54 Hypovolemia (supine to support blood pressure, keep warm, oxygen to SpO2 94% or more; PCP vascular access and fluid bolus), p.58 Acetaminophen (500 - 1,000 mg PO, not within 4 hours of a prior dose, severe liver disease), p.65 Entonox (caution: shock; baseline vital signs first), p.68 Ibuprofen (300-400 mg PO; hypersensitivity to NSAIDs, active GI hemorrhage or ulcers, pregnancy, anticoagulants), p.78 Tranexamic Acid (indications, 2 g IV push over 1 minute).
